candidates.explanation: The password-change branch of AuthService.update ends the user's other sessions. The snippet is truncated at this call, so I could not see it. It most likely passes the wrong value as the session to keep. For example, it may pass the user id (userJwtPayload.id or currentUser.id) as excludeId instead of userJwtPayload.sessionId. It may also call a plain deleteByUserId with no exclusion. In either case the current session is deleted, so the next /auth/refresh from that device fails with 401, because SessionService.updateByHash finds no session. The line range is an estimate.

I did not see this code, and the line range is a guess. If the exclusion condition here is wrong, it would produce this symptom too. Examples are using Not(...) on the wrong field, comparing against the wrong id, or filtering the wrong user. The effect would be that the current session is deleted while some other session survives. The Mongo/document repository has the same method and the same risk.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, after a successful password change, call sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude({ userId: currentUser.id, excludeId: userJwtPayload.sessionId }). The excluded id must be the session id from the JWT payload, not the user id. Also check that the repository implementations delete all sessions of that user except the one with the excluded id, with the types and field names matching.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, after a successful password change, call sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude({ userId: currentUser.id, excludeId: userJwtPayload.sessionId }). The excluded id must be the session id from the JWT payload, not the user id. Also check that the repository implementations delete all sessions of that user except the one with the excluded id, with the types and field names matching.
